clue.text: Opening of premises suitable for private occupation of the headman

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of premises

parts.note: housing that is fit for people to live in privately is residential

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blurb for premises fit to house a village chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of' takes P from premises; the rest of the wordplay is one long synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something presidential belongs to the head of a state or body, and a headman is a chief, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Appear in play on time as Wall, a low sort

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
in play means the letters are moving about, rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor appearing as Wall in a play, a lowly part like Snout's in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Wall in Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'; 'in play' rearranges APPEAR to PARAPE, set on T.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Order some orthopaedic treatment

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request for a course of bone and joint therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order or decree issued by an authority.

clue.text: Where one that's bubbly may be left to cool off

definitions.text: Where one that's bubbly may be left to cool off

parts.words: Where one that's bubbly may be left to cool off
parts.note: sounds like a place for an overexcited person to calm down, but describes chilling champagne

explanation.definitionFit: Champagne, called bubbly, is chilled in a container full of frozen water before serving.

clue.text: Ants? Rootling around, meets millions

indicators.note: rootling around is rummaging about, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Ants scurrying about who encounter millions of their fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is an old and dialect word for an ant.

clue.text: Tree in river gaining in diameter

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree growing in a river whose trunk keeps getting thicker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall; 'gaining' just adds IN and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree whose pods give a sour pulp used in cooking.

clue.text: Article about novel drained of colour

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article encloses the novel

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
She is the novel by H Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a book which has faded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is not an anagram signal: it stands for SHE, H Rider Haggard's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale as ash, with all colour gone from the face.

clue.text: International authority on racehorses is not reliable

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is an international body
a stable is a group of racehorses kept by one owner or trainer

explanation.surface: A world body that has authority over racing is untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unstable cannot be relied upon, liable to give way or change.

clue.text: Intervene as gong sounds

indicators.note: sounds says the word is said aloud and the answer is spelt differently

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: Stepping in as the dinner gong rings out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' suggests a struck instrument, but it is slang for a MEDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere or intervene uninvited in others' affairs.

clue.text: Increase in sound level

indicators.note: sound tells the solver to go by how a word is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: to level a building is to raze it to the ground

explanation.surface: A remark about turning up the volume on a stereo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increase in sound level' reads as one phrase about volume, but 'sound' is the homophone signal working on 'level' (RAZE).
explanation.definitionFit: A raise is a pay increase, and to raise something is to increase it, so either noun or verb works.

clue.text: By accident mother is struck dumb

indicators.note: by means next to, so accident sits beside mother in the answer

parts.note: mum is an everyday word for mother
a chance is an accident, something unplanned

explanation.surface: A mother who suddenly finds herself unable to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By accident' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'By' only places the accident word next to MUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumchance is an old adjective meaning silent or tongue-tied, the state of someone struck dumb.

clue.text: Drug sniffer — one looking for cups

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, a drug
a sniffer dog is one that hunts things out, a hunter

explanation.surface: A customs dog trained to find narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a customs sniffer dog; the definition is one who competes just for trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-hunter is a sportsman who enters contests chiefly to win prizes, cups being trophies.

clue.text: Scored and made a record

definitions.meaning: music that is scored is written down in notes
to make a record of something is to write it down, to note it

explanation.definitionFit: Noted means written down, whether as a musical score or as a jotted record of an event.

clue.text: Make them go away

parts.note: reads as a plea to banish some people, but 'them' stands for the word that completes the idiom 'make ... ' meaning to leave

explanation.definitionFit: To make tracks is an idiom for leaving or departing, so the word completing it means go away.

clue.text: Article cut from publication was first declared invalid

indicators.note: cut from says the article is removed from the publication word

parts.note: an annual is a yearly publication
a is the indefinite article
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A newspaper story spiked from a paper that had first ruled it void.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage or contract annulled has been officially declared void or invalid.

clue.text: Group of players in costume

definitions.meaning: a small band of musicians or actors performing together
a matching outfit of clothes worn together

explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is both a performing group and a coordinated outfit, from French for together.

clue.text: Reject opportunity to find adequate working area

parts.note: to elbow someone is to reject them, give them the elbow
room is scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: Turning down a chance of a decent place to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give someone the elbow' is British slang for rejecting or dumping them.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move or work freely.

clue.text: I, Claudius, a non-U novel, leaves one feeling like death

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
non-U says one U is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: Robert Graves's novel I, Claudius, judged vulgar, leaves a reader feeling wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper class; here 'non-U' strips a U from I CLAUDIUS, and 'novel' rearranges ICLADIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suicidal feels like dying, wanting death.

clue.text: Interpret for the Tory faithful

parts.note: Cons is an abbreviation for Conservative, the party of the Tories
someone faithful is true, loyal

explanation.surface: A request to explain things for loyal Conservative party members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tory faithful' reads as loyal party members; Cons is the standard short form of Conservatives, the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a statement is to interpret or analyse its meaning.

clue.text: Picked for one's country — or applauded when left out?

indicators.note: left out says the letter for left is removed

parts.note: applauded means clapped

explanation.surface: Selected for the national team, or merely applauded when dropped?
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player is capped when picked for the national side.
explanation.definitionFit: A capped player has been selected to represent their country, traditionally given a cap.

clue.text: This can bring one quickly down to earth

definitions.text: This can bring one quickly down to earth

parts.words: This can bring one quickly down to earth
parts.note: sounds like a reality check deflating someone, but literally describes descending a cliff on a rope

explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a rock face rapidly on a doubled rope, literally coming down to the ground.

clue.text: There is a clear case for a light here

definitions.text: There is a clear case for a light here

parts.words: There is a clear case for a light here
parts.note: reads like an argument that a lamp is needed, but a transparent casing houses a flame

explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a lamp with a transparent casing protecting the flame.

clue.text: Graduate wife in concert has 18th century hairdo

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: in says the wife letter goes inside the concert word

parts.note: a gig is a concert

explanation.surface: A graduate's wife at a concert sporting an antique hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagwig was an 18th-century wig with the back hair enclosed in a silk bag.

clue.text: In France, he's in town, there to make a spicy dish

indicators.note: in places the French pronoun inside the name of the town

parts.note: Pau is a town in south-western France
il is French for he

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in a provincial town cooking an aromatic meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' tells you the town is French too: PAU, near the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is rice cooked in stock with spices, often with meat, a dish of the Middle East and India.

clue.text: Not a success as a housemaster?

definitions.text: Not a success as a housemaster?

parts.words: Not a success as a housemaster?
parts.note: suggests a failed schoolteacher, but alludes to Poe's tale of the Fall of the House of the title family, whose master failed

explanation.definitionFit: An usher was an assistant schoolmaster, and Roderick of Poe's house was its doomed master.

clue.text: Cleaner resort for a Western monarch

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday destination fit for a cowboy king, ending with a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort, rearranging A, W and MONARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a woman employed to clean houses or offices, a domestic cleaner.

clue.text: Operatic heroine to be married soon

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A soprano character who will shortly be wed.
explanation.walkthrough: Manon is the heroine of operas by Massenet and Puccini.
explanation.definitionFit: Manon Lescaut is the heroine of Massenet's Manon and Puccini's Manon Lescaut.

clue.text: Watchdog used by John Gay's Susan?

parts.note: the watch half: to eye something is to watch it
the dog half: to dog someone is to follow or shadow them

explanation.surface: A guard dog belonging to the poet John Gay's heroine Susan.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gay wrote the ballad 'Black-Eyed Susan', so make-up for the eyes suits her, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is cosmetic colouring for the eyelids, jokingly suited to someone called black-eyed.

clue.text: Wild animal's den cut off from attack

indicators.note: cut off from says the following word is removed from the synonym of attack

parts.note: to denounce someone is to attack them publicly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beast's lair has been isolated from an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious attack word is POUNCE, but that leaves nothing for 'den'; DENOUNCE minus DEN works.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat of central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Sign in on behalf of member just after introduction

indicators.note: the sign and in pieces come immediately after the others

parts.note: pro means for, on behalf of
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an omen is a sign of things to come
something in, such as a fashion or a batsman, is on

explanation.surface: An instruction to register for someone who has just joined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' as ON is the cricket sense: the batsman who is in is on, at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolegomenon is a preliminary essay or introduction to a learned work.
